Fracture mechanisms

  • Fractures that are caused by traumatic forces
  • Fractures caused due to stress (repetitive injury)
  • Fractures caused because of certain pathology in the fractured bone

Traumatic forces types

Rotational force => Spiral fracture (long oblique fracture)

Compressing force on long axis of the bone => short oblique fracture

Crushing force on long axis of the bone => comminuted fracture (multiple fragments)

Bending force on the horizontal axis of the bone => fracture with a butterﬂy fragment or oblique fracture

Bone fragment looks like butterfly wing

Tension type of force => transverse fracture or avulse a small fragment of the bone at the point of ligament or tendon insertion.

Stress fractures

Stress fracture is a small break in the bone that occur from repetitive injury or prolonged stress applied to the bone

Occur in weight bearing bones: tibia, fibula, femur

Mechanism: repetitive stress lead to bone resorption by osteoclasts happen faster than bone formation mediated by osteoblasts

Occur in people that do heavy exercise such as runners, dancers, gymnasts.

Also occur in nutritional deficiencies of calcium and vitamin D in elderly people

Pathological fractures

Fractures that occur due to pathology in the fractured bone

Pathologies include: osteoporosis, osteogenesis imperfecta, bisphosphonate therapy, lytic bone lesions in metastasis or multiple myeloma
